main_text.p: In confirmādís autem nostrís ar‑gumentationibus , infirmandísqúe contrarijs,sepe erunt accusatori mo‑tus animorum incitandi, reo miti‑gandi.atque hæc quidem utriq; ma‑xime in peroratione facienda: alteri frequentatione argumentorum, & coaceruatione uniuersa: alteri,si pla‑nè caussam redarguendo explicarit, enumeratione, ut quicq; diluerit, & miseratione ad extremum.

In confirmandis autem nostris.) De confirma‑tione & refutatione coniecturæ, quoniam locos antea tradidit, hic de solis motibus præcipit: ut ni‑mirum accusator argumentis uehementiam & a‑crimoniam adiungat, incitandis ad iracundiam animis: defensor uero in iisdem motibus mitigâdis & sedandis intendat.

Atq; hæc quidem utriq; maxime.) De pero‑ratione actoris & rei, duo ponit præcepta: com‑mune utriusq; alterum, alterum proprium singu‑lorum. Commune illud est, ut quæ de motibus præ‑cepit in confirmatione & refutatione, ea maxime ab utroque in peroratione feruentur. Sunt enim omnia uehementiora in peroratione & conclu‑sione. Propria uero illa: accusatoris esse, frequen‑tare

page.notes: Text in smaller italic type below the main text is the commentary; the printed page is a Latin commentary page with Cicero's text in roman. Some letters are faint at the right edge of the notes and the last word "tare" is a catchword-like fragment, recorded also as catchword. Show-through and margin stains omitted.
